subject.title: Feature request: MEMORY.md size warning/limit enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw add Control UI save-time MEMORY.md budget enforcement and archive assistance, or keep the current doctor/prompt diagnostics as the supported boundary?
rationale: Current code already warns after actual truncation and doctor reports near-limit files, but refusing saves and auto-archiving workspace memory add new user workflow and ownership semantics that source inspection cannot settle.

options.title: Add bounded Control UI enforcement
options.body: Implement a visible budget meter plus warning/blocking behavior for bootstrap files, and leave archive automation for a separate scoped follow-up.

options.title: Keep diagnostics-only boundary
options.body: Treat prompt notices and doctor diagnostics as the supported behavior and narrow this issue away from save refusal or archive automation.

options.title: Sponsor broader memory lifecycle
options.body: Design archive, routing, and lifecycle semantics together with related memory-promotion work before implementing UI enforcement.

recommendation.title: Add bounded Control UI enforcement
recommendation.body: Implement a visible budget meter plus warning/blocking behavior for bootstrap files, and leave archive automation for a separate scoped follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main maintenance touches both the bootstrap diagnostics and Control UI/gateway file surfaces involved in the decision.
